summary: The critic pass is complete. Current cards retain false outcome memories, unsupported costs or skill gains, moral/gating defects and two duplicate premises; fixes are specified in the batch verdicts. Card sources were not edited.

scope.definition: Current compiled, non-retired members of the adopted evidence-gap/re-review queue. This is not a new review of every compiled card or proof of ordinary-play reachability/frequency.

issues.problem: The return letters assert the ward held, a batch was saved, or the player did not open the file. Return flags are set solely by internship performance >=80 in intern_assessment, and all three letters can be delivered without those milestone scenes ever showing. The Unseen letter can also contradict choosing to read the file.
issues.fix: Make the base letters refer to the strong placement; gate any specific accomplishment on the actual successful choice, not merely seeing its card.

issues.problem: The yes reply calls its paw print the foal’s agreement, although the letter requires only a strong placement. The foal may never have been found, or the player may have counted it and left it; neither history supplies a foal at the station.
issues.fix: Use a nonspecific station creature in the reply, or gate the foal detail on actually raising it.

issues.problem: Asking about the winters grants Vigor for reading a letter. Asking about winter courier routes likewise grants Vigor for looking at a map. Neither outcome shows stamina, reflex, duelling or flight practice.
issues.fix: Use a knowledge gain supported by the reply, or show practical preparation or flight before retaining Vigor.
evidence: docs/authoring/costs.md: skill XP follows matching practice

issues.problem: A reunion flag puts Ilse in the graduation photograph even after ilse_northern_letter sends her north. That departure sets ilse_went_north and makes her absent; the letter explicitly leaves her return by graduation uncertain. This card neither tests her departure nor explains a return.
issues.fix: Distinguish her current absence from the earlier reunion, or explicitly resolve her return before staging the photograph.

issues.problem: The pick:2 menu accepts both a print option and Strike them all. The latter says every line is removed but does not clear remember_* flags, so the fame/thesis/alignment line remains eligible for the yearbook. Both contradictory say lines are shown.
issues.fix: Make the plain-name decision exclusive through existing content wiring, or give it an unambiguous override honored by every yearbook gate; ensure selection order cannot change the result.
evidence: src/engine.js: chooseMany executes every selected option

issues.problem: The second setup says someone is rehearsing a proposal of marriage, but the matched Listen outcome says the proposal ends in a yes and that the player stole a wedding. Rehearsal has become an actual accepted proposal without a transition.
issues.fix: Keep the second outcome about overhearing the rehearsal, or change its setup to an actual proposal.

issues.problem: The card is explicitly bound to evening and closes the whole library, while the place remains open at night and several fixed character schedules put them there at night. It stages the global closing bell before ordinary permitted night visits.
issues.fix: Place closing after the last open session, or make this the closure of a specific upper gallery while the main library remains open.

issues.problem: By the third showing the painting outcome says the player is now trusted with the moving scenery. The setup also increasingly treats the player as an experienced stagehand even if every previous visit was spent taste-testing; showing the card does not earn that painting trust.
issues.fix: Gate earned stagehand experience on actually helping, or make every showing a new invitation that does not assume previous work.

issues.problem: Telling a nervous first-year the kind truth grants Lumen in addition to Charm with no sacrifice, risk or forgone duty shown. It is ordinary reassurance, which the alignment rule expressly leaves unmoralized.
issues.fix: Remove the positive alignment reward, or make the assistance involve a real cost rather than adding an unexplained penalty.

issues.problem: The final-year setup remembers sitting on this summons bench, and the options speak as an experienced visitor, but eligibility comes only from access to the tower. Access can come from rel(isolde)>=12 without ever being summoned to this bench.
issues.fix: Gate a remembered summons on the actual earlier scene, or use a final-year observation about the new student that makes no claim about the player’s history.

issues.problem: Humming along always spends Mana. The outcomes describe singing, cold hands, thin air and an unspecified cost, but never show the player casting or the tower drawing their magic. The resource cost is not the bodily effort the prose actually names.
issues.fix: Explicitly show the tower drawing magic through the tune, or use a cost that the existing scene supports.

issues.problem: This repeats the Observatory roof ledge’s full decision: climb through a high window onto a narrow exterior ledge for the view, risk a slip/gust and scraped hands, or remain at the window with a partial view. Moving it to the Seventh Tower and exchanging the sky for a castle panorama leaves the same premise, options and danger punchline.
issues.fix: Give this tower exterior a different task or consequence, such as negotiating a blocked passage or retrieving something, rather than another view-versus-window ledge dare.
evidence: content/events/pools/castle_towers.grim: observatory_roof_ledge; full opening and outcomes inspected.

issues.problem: Inventing an impressive dream deceives the lecturer on a required assignment and can receive full marks and public praise. It has no Hollow movement, although the alternative bears the honest account’s embarrassment.
issues.fix: Apply the appropriate Hollow movement to choosing the fabricated assignment, independent of whether the deception succeeds.
evidence: docs/authoring/costs.md: cheating and lying for gain

issues.problem: The first Hold the water outcome says the exercise uses all the Mana the player had, but the option always spends only -small. At ordinary larger Mana values the player retains most of their bar.
issues.fix: Describe the strain without asserting complete depletion, or condition the wording on the actual remaining resource.

issues.problem: The second setup declares the player’s clockwork wren now sings on key and hops even if the previous choice only repaired the neighbour’s entry, or the player’s own tinkering failed. Show count does not record a successful repair.
issues.fix: Keep the wren’s development independent of unchosen or failed actions, or gate the claimed improvement on the actual successful work.

issues.problem: These three cards repeat their course’s track/class/repeat/weight properties directly despite existing evocation_class, astromancy_class and alchemy_class pools. The other ordinary course cards in this same batch already join their course pools.
issues.fix: Join the existing course pool on each card and retain only intentional overrides, such as this batch’s four-month repeat.

issues.problem: The gate only requires seeing bram_duel, but that earlier card permits declining and can end in Bram winning. The rematch assumes a previous defeat drove his month of practice, and its loss says Now we’re even. Both claims can follow an earlier refusal or an earlier loss by the player.
issues.fix: Require the actual prior victory for this rematch, or branch its setup and result on the earlier fight outcome.
evidence: content/events/people_students.grim: bram_duel left Decline and right lose
content/world/facts/bram.grim: bram.rematch describes what follows his losses

issues.problem: The knows(tobias.moonflowers) branch writes that Tobias held the greenhouse door shut with his whole body in a storm. That fact unlocks from relationship >=12 and only says he would stand in a storm for the flowers. Knowing it neither witnesses nor records that specific rescue.
issues.fix: Write the recommendation from the known fact as a disposition, or gate the claimed storm scene on its actual event/choice evidence.

issues.problem: The final-warning continuity problem from finding 32 is repaired: failure now confiscates the picks instead of giving the expulsion-triggering detention. The skill/relationship problem remains: a bare coin toss decides whether a coached-sounding deception wins over Vey. No tracked ability or relationship can affect it.
issues.fix: If this is a player-assisted escape, explicitly let the player help the story and use the matching check; if it is solely Vey’s independent disposition, make that independent uncertainty the stated reason for the chance rather than presenting the roll as Corvin’s skill.
evidence: docs/authoring/checks.md: skill-sensitive actions are not bare chance

issues.problem: This card can be dealt during the day, but its opening and both outcomes already take place under the night sky, including waiting through midnight.
issues.fix: Give the card an evening/night slot or write an explicit transition that spends the remaining daylight before the stargazing.

issues.problem: One watching outcome promises that next time the wardrobe has been replaced by a teacup; repeat 6 deals the unchanged wardrobe opening again.
issues.fix: Make the next visit conditional on the earlier outcome, or remove the definite promise about the next visit.

issues.problem: Winning or drawing against the mannequin learns thorne.lost, whose fact says Thorne lost badly to a storm. Only the loss dialogue actually discloses that story. The winning and drawn tutorials silently give the player specific history Thorne never tells them.
issues.fix: Give his storm admission a line in each outcome that teaches the fact, or learn the fact only in the outcome that discloses it.

issues.problem: The first market setup always says the square is all stalls this morning, but the place card has no time/slot gate and can first be drawn on an afternoon or evening village visit.
issues.fix: Use slot-neutral wording for the recurring market, or restrict this specifically morning version and preserve an appropriate counter for later visits.

issues.problem: Let them come to lectures always puts the silver bees through a live Astromancy lecture. The ownership/season gate excludes winter but not summer breaks spent at the castle, when the ambient card can still be dealt and ordinary classes are suspended.
issues.fix: Require term for the lecture version, or give the break version an activity the player can actually attend.

issues.problem: Finding 7 is only partly repaired. The new seen(corvin_confiscation_vault)>0 gate proves a vault visit, but Keep lookout can fail with the alarm and detention and never retrieve the deck. The new card still places the grandfather’s deck in Corvin’s hands after that failed recovery.
issues.fix: Require evidence of an actual retrieval, or use an ordinary deck until it exists. Do not treat seeing the vault or learning its fact as proof of the successful outcome.

issues.problem: Stand beside Corvin says nobody has ever stood next to him, although corvin_brother can already have ended with the player literally standing beside him to face the brother down. Honest for Once likewise calls the brother/money admission the first time he has told anyone, although the earlier gates scene explicitly tells the player all of it.
issues.fix: Acknowledge the earlier disclosure and support when known/chosen, keeping first-time lines only for histories where they are true.
evidence: content/events/people_students.grim: corvin_brother text and left win

issues.problem: Pay him to go says the player gives everything in their purse, but always subtracts gold -large. A player with more than that retains money; one with less cannot choose the option, rather than giving what they have.
issues.fix: Describe paying the demanded amount instead of emptying the purse, or implement an actual whole-purse payment if intended.

issues.problem: Paying the threatening brother to leave moves the player Hollow. The scene shows a costly attempt to protect someone from an extorter; it does not show greed, cheating, exploitation or another moral wrong by the payer. Corvin disliking the method is already a relationship issue and does not establish a Hollow act.
issues.fix: Remove the unsupported moral penalty, or show the harmful bargain the player is knowingly choosing.

issues.problem: Random repeat outcomes repeatedly claim a unique first: Seraphine is glad to be wrong for the first time, Gerald has never patted a nose even Tobias’s, and Lyra lets the player walk her back for the first time. The same random branch can recur next showing and deny the earlier occurrence.
issues.fix: Put first-time discoveries in a true sequence/state gate, and write later outcomes as established intimacy rather than repeating the milestone.

issues.problem: Walking close under the enormous umbrella always costs Health, but neither outcome describes getting wet, cold, exerted or hurt. The contrasting race explicitly gets the player drenched and has no Health cost, making the supposed protection the unexplained bodily loss.
issues.fix: Remove the unsupported Health loss or show the actual exposure paid under the umbrella.

issues.problem: Pin it up, for later grants study readiness, but both outcomes only hang up an invention plan and discuss building it later. No revision, coursework or exam practice is done.
issues.fix: Show using the saved time for coursework, or remove the unrelated study gain while retaining the relationship payoff.

issues.problem: The setup starts the visit at midnight, but the first Stay and finish outcome says both are asleep by eleven. The short continuation runs backward in clock time.
issues.fix: Use a time after midnight or avoid the hour.

issues.problem: The first Leave a lock open outcome calls this the player’s first lock. The earlier corvin_lock_lesson can already have taught and successfully completed one, as can several other lock scenes.
issues.fix: Say a lock rather than your first lock, or test the established history.

issues.problem: These fixed-character cards repeat every four to seven months but have no changing text/say variants. The ex cards restage the same canvas, retraction or lock encounter after the player already chose or failed it; the gift and lesson jokes likewise replay unchanged. They miss the repeat requirement for several variation points and outcomes that remain fresh at the fourth showing.
issues.fix: Add matched repeat variants that respect previous outcomes, or make genuinely singular gifts/apologies/lessons one-time scenes while retaining a separate recurring situation.

issues.problem: The thorn-wand temptation repeats the Siphon lesson: a tired student alone by the dormitory windowsill considers draining a potted fern; accepting greys the fern and makes the player feel wonderful. The item wrapper changes the resource reward but leaves the same staged temptation and resolution.
issues.fix: Give the thorn wand a different temptation and victim/context, or make it a conditional continuation of the earlier fern scene rather than independently staging it again.

issues.problem: Tracing the old duel loses Mood, but every outcome describes a bodily cost: aching knees, tiring footwork, or standing up stiff. None shows boredom, humiliation, worry or another loss of spirits.
issues.fix: Use the shown exertion cost, or show the emotional cost consistently if Mood is intended.

issues.problem: The third setup says the player has started leaving both cups washed and Maud has rewarded that habit with a biscuit. A player who always weeds the beds instead leaves the tea untouched and has never chosen the tea-and-cup-washing outcome.
issues.fix: Record actual cup washing before claiming the habit, or anchor the third setup on Maud’s preparations rather than an unchosen action.

issues.problem: The first setup explicitly addresses the available note for whoever’s next, inviting a reader. Reading it nonetheless always moves Hollow and describes guilty snooping. The moral trespass is absent from that variant’s open invitation.
issues.fix: Distinguish a public invitation from private correspondence in the choice and effects, or make every variant clearly private before assigning the Hollow cost.

issues.problem: Go and find her charges Health, while its outcome only walks to the open office behind the ward. No exertion, exposure, lost sleep or other bodily cost is shown.
issues.fix: Remove the unsupported Health charge or describe the actual physical cost of finding her.

issues.problem: The shared suffix sets red_ink_glimpse after both success and failure. Failure says the player slept through the collection, but the next card recognizes the robes from the stair and the journal says the player saw the first-year take the essay.
issues.fix: Record the visual glimpse only on success; use a separate progress condition to advance the thread after a failed stakeout.

issues.problem: Hiding on a landing to identify an ordinary first-year collecting an essay is pitched at master-. Nothing in the scene supplies a faculty-level observer or ward; the actual obstacle is an unprepared peer.
issues.fix: Pitch the stealth attempt at the peer and stairwell, using only the difficulty and circumstance adjustments the scene supports.
evidence: docs/authoring/checks.md: mundane/peer ladder and obstacle rule

issues.problem: The failed objection leaves the first-year seated without reading, then sets red_ink_finished. That flag stamps the journal line On Thursday she spoke, all the way to the end, reporting the opposite result.
issues.fix: Give the journal a result-sensitive line or separate completion from successful speaking.

issues.problem: The campus mini-plots queue later months without a term/presence deferral. Starting near a term end can put the player in the academy ward, stairwell or classroom during a break spent at home or on internship. Queue delivery does not infer those restrictions from the original start card.
issues.fix: Defer the campus steps while the player is away and require teaching months for actual class/seminar scenes; preserve the queued step instead of dropping it with a false when.
evidence: src/engine.js: advance checks only each queued card’s own when/defer
home_cottage_bloomer_father and home_market_bloomer_charm show the existing defer pattern

issues.problem: Leaving the practice candle subtracts study even though the outcome only gives her a used candle and receives a drawing later. No missed work or revision is described.
issues.fix: Remove the study charge or show the revision time actually sacrificed; do not treat gifting a non-inventory keepsake as lost study.

issues.problem: The failed Talk her down route charges Health, but its outcome only says an hour, three kettles and a carter’s story. It shows delay and embarrassment without bodily exertion or injury.
issues.fix: Show the physical cost of carrying hot water or freeing the arm, or use the cost the outcome actually depicts.

issues.problem: Read what people lose explicitly reads private love letters and notes in other people’s pockets for useful gossip, but treats this as an ordinary Guile/pay option without the privacy violation’s Hollow consequence used by lantern_washed_up.
issues.fix: Add the modest Hollow consequence for knowingly reading private correspondence, or restrict the inspection to public names and lending marks.

issues.problem: Ask what you could have done better grants Vigor at the Field Station, although all that happens is listening to a twenty-minute report and writing notes on the coach. Vigor requires bodily practice.
issues.fix: Show a last practical demonstration/repeated exercise for the Field Station branch, or use a learning reward grounded in reading the report.

issues.problem: Planting in Maud’s secret frost-free garden sets the same flag as Tobias’s greenhouse. Later cards put the plant beside Gerald and the warm greenhouse pipes, threaten it with frost, and have it bolt across the greenhouse. The chosen garden is forgotten.
issues.fix: Remember the planting location and adapt the later scenes, or have Maud offer a protected spot inside the same greenhouse so both routes converge honestly.

issues.problem: The opening credits the fisherman with explaining that you must beat the gulls, even when you skipped his conversation or failed the appeal and heard only fish talk.
issues.fix: Branch on tailwind_fisherman, or make the loft master/jar supply the race clue independently.

issues.problem: Take the jar down grants Vigor, but only taking a jar off a shelf and holding it is shown; all the actual flight is in the other option or later cards.
issues.fix: Show a first physical test flight/wind exercise in the accepting outcome, or remove the exertion reward.

issues.problem: Birthday and poets’ supper sequences explicitly move forward a year on their second showing, but repeat 3 is a turn cooldown and neither card has an annual gate. They can be selected again three months later, and even more than once within the same academic year.
issues.fix: Track the last year offered and allow one showing per year, or make later showings ordinary reunions/suppers without another birthday or last-year claim.

issues.problem: The second opening says the president remembers your contest verdict from last year, even if you only poured and listened on the first showing.
issues.fix: Gate the remembered verdict on choosing Judge; otherwise recall your serving or listening.

issues.problem: Everything on one hand and its loss outcomes say all earlier winnings are lost, but the fixed gold -large is only thirty crowns; two preceding wins have added substantially more. The gamble leaves earlier profits while telling the player they lost them all.
issues.fix: Either describe the actual fixed stake and retained earlier winnings, or explicitly store and stake the night’s profit if the intended bet is everything.

issues.problem: With ring_last_standing the only noncombat option is locked. The opener advertises the contract, so this is deliberate, but it contradicts the standing every-fight-has-a-nonfight-route checklist; the same issue is recorded for the cameos.
issues.fix: Offer a costly surrender/forfeiture route during last standing, or explicitly record and approve the intended design exception in PROGRESS.md.

issues.problem: Let it happen grants Charm for hiding under the table and watching the food fight. The player does not persuade, perform, talk to or guide anyone.
issues.fix: Keep the Mood reward and remove Charm, or show the player actively joining/organizing a social exchange that earns it.

issues.problem: At Illusion II the practical makes three people falsely remember the player rescuing the cook. This knowingly takes undeserved credit through manipulated memories but has no Hollow consequence, unlike other lying-for-gain choices.
issues.fix: Give this level-specific fabrication its moral consequence, or make it an openly consented classroom illusion test that does not create real false credit.

issues.problem: The right label is always Watch how the hare moves even when the advanced setup and outcome are about a hawk or hippogriff.
issues.fix: Use a species-neutral label such as Study its movement first, or branch the label with the course level.

issues.problem: Declining the lesson leaves this repeat-4 offer eligible, but each opening again claims I’ve never shown anyone after the player has already watched her demonstrate it.
issues.fix: Branch the opening on seen(lyra_teaches_wildfire), with a repeat invitation after the first showing.

issues.problem: The level-I opening says Illusion begins by trying to make Vey like the student, and the left route casts directly on her. The worldbook fact vey.own_face says every student first glamours their own face, because a glamour they cannot hold on themselves will not hold on anyone.
issues.fix: Put the required self-glamour step before trying it on Vey in the introductory practical, or change the introductory exercise to match the established teaching order.

issues.problem: Play her honestly warns that she may take the player’s purse, but the appeal loss always grants a small tip. There is no stake deduction or purse-loss path. The button promises a financial risk the card never executes.
issues.fix: Describe the actual risk of a smaller tip and embarrassment, or implement the intended monetary downside with matching outcomes.

issues.problem: Let her win moves Hollow even though the setup says she always knows when someone lets her win and every outcome confirms she knows. The described exchange is a paid, mutually understood performance; no cheating victim or deception for gain is established.
issues.fix: Remove the Hollow shift from the consensual performance, or establish an actual deceptive or exploitative choice if that is intended.

issues.problem: On the third showing the crowd parts for the player as the cat-retrieval expert even if every prior choice was Wait him out and the cat came down by himself. The sequence awards a successful-rescuer reputation without checking any rescue.
issues.fix: Gate expert status on a successful climb, or let the crowd recognize a familiar onlooker instead.

issues.problem: Every cameo locks its only non-fight choice when ring_last_standing is set. The opener can set that flag before queuing a cameo, so the additional encounter presents only a fight. This violates the current checklist’s rule that each fight sits beside a route without a fight, even though entering the ring earlier was optional.
issues.fix: Keep a costly walkout/concession route available on the cameo, including last-standing nights, or explicitly record an approved design exception instead of silently contradicting the fight rule.
evidence: content/events/pools/night.grim: ring_on_yourself on_show and win queues

issues.problem: Say you’d had it too knowingly fabricates nearly supporting notes to retain credit and avoid reputational loss. The new Deceive check correctly makes it skill-sensitive, but still grants no Hollow consequence; the more aggressive smear option does.
issues.fix: Add the modest Hollow consequence to the dishonest denial before its check.

issues.problem: Deliver it as asked charges Study but only shows finding the recipient in the library and carrying a short reply. The revised writing-help route shows the time spent; the delivery route does not show any displaced coursework.
issues.fix: Add the missed reading/essay time to the delivery outcome, or use a trade that the errand actually shows.

issues.problem: These routes still use bare chance for demonstrating learned knowledge, interpreting a task, defending a research opinion, brewing a heating reaction, persuading an astronomer, estimating a creature count, feeding a hostile patient or reading covert social cues. Current checks.md requires a skill-sensitive check when the relevant expertise or relationship can plausibly change the outcome; none can affect these rolls.
issues.fix: Replace each bare chance with the appropriately pitched plain research/brew/appeal/soothe/deceive check (and a circumstance step where justified), retaining genuinely random environmental events as chance.
evidence: docs/authoring/checks.md: pure luck versus skill-sensitive attempts

issues.problem: The second Take the near shelves outcome says everyone knows the player has never been below the third landing. The first showing can have successfully completed the deep request down four hundred steps. Choosing near shelves now cannot erase that earlier work.
issues.fix: Describe today’s easy requests without claiming the player has never done a deep one, or check actual previous choices.

issues.problem: The third setup awards the binder’s trust with older pages regardless of repeated failed repairs or always watching rather than mending. Its journeyman+ steady check also uses the low-rung repeat pattern that checks.md explicitly advises against because later expertise nearly removes its risk.
issues.fix: Gate earned repair trust on performance or successful work, and use normal swing unless the repeat is intentionally a documented measure the player outgrows.

issues.problem: The third setup says the player has carried instruments up this ridge so often the goats ignore them. A player who always chose the sums in the tent never carried those instruments; the card’s show count advances anyway.
issues.fix: Anchor the sequence on the expedition’s routine or gate the carrying history on actual participation.

issues.problem: The third setup calls the player the station’s best counter because they stopped minding damp, even after always making the estimate by the stove or repeatedly giving inaccurate counts. No performance or successful count gate supports that reputation.
issues.fix: Condition the earned reputation on the work, or make the third setup about the station’s recurring dawn count rather than the player’s unearned proficiency.

issues.problem: Every failed test spends Health, but the three outcomes only change the player’s fringe, robe folds or a scorch mark on the wall. The card does not show bodily harm or exposure corresponding to that cost.
issues.fix: Show the actual physical effect of the failed spell in each variant, or replace the Health charge with the consequence the scene depicts.

issues.problem: The Glamour options magically manipulate another person for a benefit: bypassing the boatman’s rental price, erasing a prefect’s intended sanction, and obtaining a reserved parcel. The prose explicitly makes them forget or misremember why they like the player, but none of these choices moves alignment. This is the dishonest/exploitative shortcut described in costs.md, not ordinary persuasion.
issues.fix: Give the manipulative shortcut its appropriate Hollow movement, or rewrite it as informed, consensual magical assistance while preserving the trade.
evidence: docs/authoring/costs.md: deception or exploitation for gain
src/engine.js: chargeCast charges Mana, and only forbidden spells automatically move alignment

issues.problem: Arrive late, quietly always loses study and mood. Running costs nothing before the roll; winning grants Vigor, while losing only loses the same study. Every running result is at least as good as walking, so the random check disguises a dominated ordinary option.
issues.fix: Give walking a real calm/rest benefit, or give the failed run a distinct cost that the late walk avoids; keep both outcomes grounded in the prose.

issues.problem: Both visit cards describe a live lecture but have no term gate. They remain in the Lecture Tower’s visit pool and spell appointments during breaks spent on campus, when ordinary classes are suspended.
issues.fix: Gate live-lecture versions to teaching months or supply an explicitly extracurricular break version.
evidence: compiled event when is absent for both cards

issues.problem: The first left outcome always calls the yard frozen, but the repeatable card can first show in summer and has no seasonal gate or wording for that detail.
issues.fix: Make the yard’s frozen state winter-dependent, or use an all-season effort cost such as carrying the heavy coal buckets.

issues.problem: Lending the scarf and leaving always loses Mood, but the outcomes describe a cold neck, a returned scarf, and a friendly joke and wave. They do not show disappointment, guilt or other loss of spirits; the concrete cost is exposure on the walk home.
issues.fix: Use the bodily exposure the scene actually shows or state the emotional cost consistently in all variants.

issues.problem: The safe Ward rescue earns Lumen for spending Mana, while stepping bodily between the swan and the first-year earns none despite the explicitly shown injury risk. The same card applies the costly-protection rule only to the safe magical route.
issues.fix: Apply the protection choice’s moral effect consistently before the physical check, or establish a concrete moral distinction between the two rescues.

issues.problem: The second setup says the children have talked of nothing else since last time and asks the player to come back. The third brings children in paper wizard hats. A player who always bought the schoolmistress tea never visited her class, so the second showing invents the visit whose payoff it celebrates.
issues.fix: Gate the remembered classroom visit on actually choosing it, or make each request the schoolmistress’s continuing invitation.

issues.problem: On later showings Mabel treats the player as the brave experimental-cake tester and serves it unasked even when every earlier choice was Stick with your usual. Showing the card does not earn the trial reputation.
issues.fix: Let Mabel remember the actual tasting choice, or retain her recurring attempt to recruit a reluctant tester without claiming an earned reputation.

issues.problem: Playing the regulars’ domino game is a bare chance even roll. Unlike the knucklebones card, this is a game where reading the board, remembering played tiles and opponents’ habits plausibly matter; the player’s skills cannot affect it.
issues.fix: Use a suitably pitched skill-sensitive wager with luck swing, preserving the pot and loss as outcomes.

issues.problem: The second setup and later outcomes remember the tubs turning the player’s robes pink last time. The first successful charm keeps the robes clean and the hand-washing route never risks discoloration. The remembered failure is not earned by either history.
issues.fix: Condition the pink-robe memory on an actual discoloration outcome, or describe the tubs’ reputation without assigning that failure to the player.

issues.problem: The second honest outcome gives the same true answer as last time, the third calls honesty a habit, and the third lie says the player lies again. The sequence advances after either choice, so switching sides produces false memories of earlier truth or deception.
issues.fix: Make each answer stand on its own, or read the actual earlier choice when describing the habit.

issues.problem: The third Hop on outcome grants Lore, but only describes going shoeless and calling it a fashion. The earlier variants explicitly earn their Lore by notes or reading; that learning disappears from the sticky variant while its reward remains.
issues.fix: Show the lecture or reading in the third outcome too, or use a scene-supported gain for that variant.

issues.problem: These two cards copy the ambient group’s class/repeat/weight setup instead of joining the world_more_routine pool already declared in their file. Their special repeat values can be intentional overrides, but the shared wiring is still duplicated.
issues.fix: Join world_more_routine and retain the different repeat values and their own gates/cast/slot as explicit overrides.
